issues.issue: The exclusion bars earth movement "whether sudden or gradual," while the EARTH MOVEMENT COVERAGE endorsement (Form RM1106) buys back sudden earth movement at scheduled locations; the two must be read together to know what is excluded.
The flat flood exclusion is contradicted in part by the FLOOD COVERAGE endorsement (Form RM1108), which insures flood at scheduled locations with its own limits and deductibles.

The fungus exclusion, with an ensuing-specified-peril exception, must be squared with the Fungus Cleanup Expense extension (Form RM1002 A.10), which pays fungus cleanup following a covered fire or lightning loss.

"Pollution" as defined reaches the presence of any "irritant or contaminant," so the one-word exclusion is capable of swallowing ordinary property damage such as smoke or dust; its intended boundary is genuinely disputable.
The blanket exclusion sits against the Pollution Cleanup Expense extension (Form RM1002 A.15), which pays to remove pollutants following specified and other insured perils.

This exclusion of demolition cost, operation of building laws and increased construction cost directly contradicts the Demolition Cost, Increased Construction Cost and Operation of Building Laws extension (Form RM1002 B.6), for which a $1,000,000 sublimit is shown on the Declarations, and contains no exception for it.
The exclusion lists specific utilities and then adds "or any other service," leaving the catch-all's reach against the enumerated specifics uncertain.
It is qualified by the INTERRUPTION OF SERVICES COVERAGE EXTENSION (Form RM1110), which insures the very off-premises service failures this paragraph excludes.
The exclusion repeatedly closes with "any other electronic equipment, computerized equipment, or similar device," a catch-all whose reach beyond the enumerated computer items is unsettled.
"Unexplained or mysterious disappearance" is not defined and its line against covered theft depends entirely on how much explanation a loss has.

The clause breaks off mid-sentence ("voluntarily relinquishes possession of covered property with or without your"), so the condition on which the exclusion turns is missing; the exclusion of "any criminal, fraudulent or dishonest acts" by "you" or your agents is also broad enough to be read against much ordinary conduct.

An exclusion for "delay, loss of market, loss of use, indirect or remote loss" cannot easily be reconciled with the Loss of Business Income and Extra Expense coverages in Form RM1001 C. and D., which insure precisely that kind of consequential loss.

The exclusion of "wear and tear, deterioration ... inherent vice, latent defect" and of "settling, cracking, shrinking, bulging" of roofs and walls, followed by an ensuing-loss exception, is the classic battleground over whether storm damage to aging building components is excluded deterioration or a covered loss.

The exclusion of machinery failure or breakdown is disapplied by Form RM1001 E.1 wherever the loss results from an "accident" to a covered "object," so its residual scope depends on those definitions.

The exclusion for "faulty, defective or inadequate" construction, workmanship, maintenance or design, coupled with the ensuing-loss exception, requires a line to be drawn between the excluded defect and the covered resulting damage.

The vehicle item both declares highway vehicles beyond 1,000 feet "not covered" and then treats other insurance as "your primary coverage," language that implies this policy does respond in excess; the two halves of the same item point in different directions.

The default replacement-cost valuation is qualified by A.2 (no replacement cost until repair, actual cash value after two years) and by the Vacancy condition, so the operative measure of loss depends on reconciling several provisions.

The clause withholds replacement cost "until the lost or damaged property is actually repaired or replaced" and cuts it off after two years, without saying how that interacts with an insured whose claim is denied and who cannot fund repairs. The trigger and the running of the two years are both open to argument.

It is in tension with the Declarations statement that "this policy provides coverage on a replacement cost basis" and with VALUATIONS A.3, which lets an insured who elects not to rebuild still claim replacement cost.
"Failure to use reasonable speed to repair, rebuild or replace" supplies no timetable, so the amount of any deduction for delay is left at large.
This permits a replacement-cost claim where the insured does not rebuild, which sits awkwardly with A.2's rule that replacement cost is not paid until the property is actually repaired or replaced.
"The proper proportion of overhead charges" gives no method of allocation and is inherently contestable.
"The value blank" is an undefined term of art for valuing damaged records, and its meaning where no blank equivalent exists is unclear.

This makes appraisal available on the unilateral demand of "either party," whereas the KANSAS CHANGES endorsement (Form RM1815) deletes and replaces it with a clause under which "an appraisal will be made only if both parties agree, voluntarily," and extends the appraiser-naming period from thirty to sixty days. Whether appraisal can be compelled turns on which text governs.

Paragraph 2 survives the KANSAS CHANGES endorsement, which replaces only paragraphs 1 and 3, leaving a court-appointed-umpire mechanism attached to an appraisal that under the Kansas text happens only by mutual consent.

This paragraph is deleted and replaced by the KANSAS CHANGES endorsement (Form RM1815) B.3, whose replacement text appears in mutilated form; which version fixes the binding effect of an award is contestable.

The rule that a breach at one location does not affect other locations is hard to reconcile with Condition I, which makes "this entire policy" void for concealment or fraud, and with the Vacancy condition's location-specific sanctions.

This sixty-day threshold for cancellation "for any reason" is deleted and replaced by ninety days in the KANSAS CHANGES — CANCELLATION endorsement (Form RM1915), so the policy states two different periods.

This paragraph and its list of cancellation grounds are deleted and replaced by the KANSAS CHANGES — CANCELLATION endorsement (Form RM1915), which substitutes a ninety-day threshold and a different list of grounds.
The bar on any change except by written endorsement is in tension with Condition K, Liberalization, under which a broadening state filing automatically alters the terms without any endorsement.
The reduction for amounts "collected from others" overlaps Condition Q, Other Insurance, and Condition X, Subrogation, which allocate third-party recoveries on different terms.
The voiding provision lists three actors and four subjects but its numbering restarts, and it is unclear whether the fraud of "any insured" voids coverage for innocent additional named insureds.

It is deleted and replaced for Kansas property by the KANSAS CHANGES endorsement (Form RM1815) I, which forfeits only loss "caused by or resulting from" the fraudulent act rather than voiding the entire policy.
